correctness.rationale: The one-hot active symbols across k strings bound the average Dirac-zero Wasserstein cost by 1/k for each n. At ends of enormously dominant active blocks, one orbit converges empirically to the all-one Dirac and the rest to the all-zero Dirac, forcing every single prototype to average error at least 1/k (including equality boundary by strict <). The O(s) transition windows up to n occupy o(n), hence empirical measures approximate convex Dirac mixtures with parameters p_{j,n}. Each p_{j,n} has subsequential limits zero and one and increments at most 1/(n+1); all intermediate limits occur. The full Wasserstein cluster segment has length one; N arbitrary off-segment prototype balls cover at most 2Nr length at radius r, attained by midpoints. Strict threshold gives floor(1/(2 epsilon))+1. No small-tolerance first-emergence counts beyond the single-prototype threshold are implied.
